extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and IP practitioners dealing with Korean patent term extension (KIPO/Intellectual Property Trial & Appeal Board)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, calculation, allowable delays, exceptions, and procedural requirements for applying for patent term extension in Korea where registration was delayed. Covers what counts as 'periods of delay attributable to an applicant', how to compute the extension, application contents, deadlines and evidentiary attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-term extension calculation formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual extension equals '(the length of the period between the reference date for extension and the date of registration of a patent right) – (the length of the period delayed due to reasons attributable to an applicant)'. Only when the length of a period exceeds zero after calculation, it shall become eligible for extension of a patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the gross delay (registration date minus reference date) then subtract all periods deemed 'attributable to an applicant'. If result ≤ 0, no extension. Be precise in calculating each component period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date for extension is 'the date four years after the filing date of a patent application or the date three years from the date of requesting examination, whichever is later.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining the reference date, for divisional/converted applications or applications filed by a legitimate right holder, certain filing dates may be deemed the filing date (see guidance on divisional/international applications). Use actual filing/entry dates where specified in the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal scope of the new extension system (eligibility by filing date)
rubrics_metrics.description: The newly-introduced system for extending patent term due to a delay in registration shall be applied only to patent applications filed after the KORUS FTA takes effect, i.e., to patent applications filed after March 15, 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications filed after March 15, 2012 are potentially eligible for extension under this system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition – 'periods of delay attributable to an applicant'
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays attributable to an applicant mean that procedural delays are caused by an applicant; it does not necessarily refer to the case that an applicant is responsible for all the delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 7-2 of the Enforcement Decree and Article 54-5 of the Enforcement Rules enumerate specific types of procedural delays attributable to an applicant (totaling many subparagraphs). Even if a period falls under those enumerated items, it may be exempted if objectively recognized not attributable to the applicant considering specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant extension/extension of designated periods counted as delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant extends the period for filing a petition for a trial or the designated period for a patent-related proceeding, the length of the extended period shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant. Where an applicant extends the period and then shortens it, the length of the shortened period shall not be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant requests and obtains an extension, that extension time is deducted from the extension calculation. If applicant later shortens the requested period, don't count the shortened amount as delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption/suspension due to applicant circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent-related proceeding (examination, trial, etc.) is interrupted or suspended due to circumstances of an applicant (e.g., applicant dies while application is pending), the period between interruption and resumption shall be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include periods of inactivity caused by applicant's personal/corporate circumstances unless objective grounds later justify exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated reporting period for consultation under Article 36(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more patent applications on the same invention are filed on the same day and the Commissioner orders an applicant to report the result of consultation within a designated period, the designated period shall constitute 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'. Where the designated period is shortened at the request of an applicant, the shortened length shall not be deemed the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If KIPO sets a reporting deadline to resolve double-filing issues, that time is attributable to applicant; voluntary shortening by applicant is not counted as delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment orders on formalities/documents counted as delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commissioner or a presiding administrative patent judge orders amendment on irregularities in formalities (Article 46) or amendment on documents (Article 203(2)), the period designated while ordering amendments shall be deemed 'the period attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments are required because applicant submitted defective formalities or failed to pay fees, the time allowed to amend is counted as applicant delay. Exception: if order and subsequent proceedings are completed prior to a request for examination so registration is not delayed, then the designated period is not deemed applicant delay. If an amendment order was mistakenly made and KIPO later recognizes no irregularity, that period may not be deemed applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim withdrawn or deemed withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examination on an application is withheld on the ground that it is a basis of domestic priority claim under Article 55(1) and then examination is no longer withheld because the priority claim is withdrawn or considered withdrawn, the period during which examination was withheld shall be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periods of examination-withholding attributable to applicant's withdrawal of priority are counted as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in determination of expedited examination due to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where determination on whether an application is to be subject to expedited examination is delayed due to circumstances of an applicant (e.g., KIPO orders amendment on request for expedited examination or attached documents), the designated period shall be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'. However, if it is later found there were no deficiencies, the designated period shall not be deemed applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent to cure applicant deficiencies in expedited-exam requests is counted unless KIPO later finds the request was fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period allowed for submission of written arguments after notice of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner notifies a ground of rejection and gives an applicant an opportunity to submit arguments under Article 63, the period allowed for submission of a written argument shall be deemed to be 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner later decides to grant a patent because the written argument traversed the rejection without other measures, then the period designated for submission shall not constitute applicant delay. The same applies when a patent administrative judge gives such opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late payment of patent fee after service of certified copy of decision to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The period between the date of service of a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent and the date when the patent right is registered after payment of the patent fee shall constitute 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant' (including additional payments after the payment period has elapsed). Where applicant is exempt from payment under Article 83, the period between service and the date when the applicant is exempt after submitting required documents shall be deemed applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay in paying fees after grant notification is counted as applicant delay, even if the applicant pays late or requires exemption processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reexamination after service of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant amended specification or drawings and made a request for reexamination, the period between the date of service of a certified copy of a decision to reject a patent application and the date when a request for reexamination is made shall be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant could have addressed rejection without reexamination and instead requested reexamination, the intervening time is applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in service of documents due to applicant (unclear address etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where service of documents is delayed because the address or business location of an applicant/representative is unclear, the length of delay for service of documents shall be 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: applicant fails to report a change of address and a decision copy is returned; the period between when applicant would have received it had they reported the change and when they actually received it counts as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination at applicant's request
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examination is deferred at the request of an applicant, the period between the date when the applicant made the request and the date when the desired expiration date of deferral occurs shall be 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant'. If the applicant withdraws the deferral request, only the period until withdrawal is deemed applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested deferrals are fully counted unless withdrawn (then count only until withdrawal) or otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of applicant-attributable delays in litigation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In litigation proceedings appealing trial decisions or similar, delays attributable to an applicant include: (1) period when a disqualification/recusal request by applicant is not accepted (time from request to rejection/decision or suspension), (2) designated periods to amend litigation capabilities/representation or complaints pursuant to court orders, (3) period between missed hearing date and newly-designated hearing date when presiding judge resets hearing because applicant failed to appear or argue, (4) period between request for evidential documents and date when such evidence is recognized not necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These litigation delays are treated analogously to KIPO proceeding delays when calculating patent-term extension; include Commission-ordered amendment periods or designated supplemental document submission periods in administrative appeal contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: applicant-caused requests/amendments/submissions count as delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods delayed due to a request, amendment or submission made by an applicant in a patent-related proceeding, a litigation proceeding regarding a trial decision or ruling, or an administrative appeal or litigation shall be deemed 'the period of delay attributable to an applicant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad principle: any procedural time taken because of applicant action/inaction is typically deducted from extension eligibility unless a specific exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to periods of delay attributable to an applicant (exemptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a period falls under enumerated applicant-attributable delays, it shall not be deemed such if: i) such delay occurred before the request for examination and did not affect delay in registration, ii) the amendment order or notification was made by mistake of the Korean Intellectual Property Office, iii) the delay was caused by other reasons such as natural disasters, not by an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: amendments completed before examination request (case i), KIPO's mistaken amendment order or later recognition that no irregularity existed (case ii), or force majeure events (case iii). Parties should document objective grounds when claiming exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents and filing deadline for registration of extension (Article 92-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of patent term extension must state: 1) name and domicile of applicant (or corporate name and office), 2) name and domicile/location of agent if any (or firm name and designated attorney), 3) patent number whose term is subject to extension, 4) the period of application for extension, 5) grounds for extension prescribed by Ordinance (materials substantiating such grounds attached). The application shall be filed within three months from the date of registration of a patent right. Where a patent is owned by joint owners, application must be filed by all joint owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict three-month filing deadline from registration. Include evidentiary materials proving grounds and attach power of attorney if represented. Joint ownership requires joint filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may amend matters falling under items 4 (period of application) and 5 (grounds for extension) before an examiner decides whether patent term extension shall be registered. However, after receiving a notice of grounds for rejection (Article 93 applied mutatis mutandis), amendment of such matters is only permitted during the period for submission of arguments following the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend early if needed; amendments after notice of rejection are constrained to the argument-submission window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written application form and required attachments (Enforcement Rules Article 54-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person filing for registration of extension must submit a written application of Annexed Form 30-2 to the Commissioner of KIPO with: 1) ground for extension and a copy of the evidential document of the extension ground, 2) power of attorney where a representative conducts the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed form (Form 30-2) and attach documentary evidence proving the extension ground; include a power of attorney if proceeding via an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated grounds for extension under Enforcement Rules Article 54-3
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for extension designated under Ordinance include: 1) the patent was registered after four years from the filing date or three years from the date of request for examination, whichever comes later; 2) the period of request for extension and an explanation that the period of delay attributable to an applicant is reduced from that period together with evidential document; 3) other necessary items to prove the ground for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that registration occurred past the reference date and document any applicant-attributable delays that must be subtracted; include any additional proof requested by Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of applicant-attributable periods where objective ground not attributable to applicant exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there exists an objective ground which is not attributable to an applicant, among grounds for delaying registration under Article 92-2(1) of the Act, the relevant period shall be reduced from a period under paragraph (1), notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part of the overall delay was due to objective reasons (e.g., administrative error, force majeure), those periods may be removed from the applicant-attributable deduction. Provide evidence to support such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of divisional/converted/international applications for reference date calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing dates of a divisional application, a converted application and an application filed by a legitimate right holder shall be the filing date of the parent application (or the filing date of application by an unentitled person); for an international application, the international filing date shall be the filing date. However, for extension calculations the actual filing date of a divisional, converted application, application by a legitimate right holder, or the date for submission of documents under Article 203(1) shall be deemed 'the filing date of a patent application'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating 'four years after the date of filing', use the actual filing date of the specific application form as required by the Enforcement Decree/Rules; periods spent by applicant choice (gap between parent filing and divisional filing or national phase entry) are treated as applicant delay.
